Spastic diplegia A common manifestation of cerebral palsy. It primarily affects the legs, although there may be considerable asymmetry between the two sides. The commonest pattern consists of o Hip flexion and internal rotation, due to overactivity by the ilipsoas, rectus femoris and hip adductors. o Knee flexion, due to overactivity of the hamstrings, especially on the medial side o Equines deformity of the foot and eversion of the hindfoot, due to overactivity by the triceps surae and peronei.
